The **2014 Indian Premier League season** (abbreviated as **IPL 7** or **Pepsi IPL 2014**) was the seventh season of the [Indian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Premier_League "Indian Premier League"), a professional Twenty20 cricket league established by the [Board of Control for Cricket in India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Control_for_Cricket_in_India "Board of Control for Cricket in India") (BCCI) in 2007. The tournament featured [eight teams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League_squads "2014 Indian Premier League squads"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-1) one fewer than in 2013 after the withdrawal of the [Pune Warriors India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pune_Warriors_India "Pune Warriors India"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-3) and was held from 16 April 2014 to 1 June 2014. The opening ceremony was held in the [UAE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates") on 15 April 2014. [Kolkata Knight Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Knight_Riders "Kolkata Knight Riders") won the tournament, defeating [Kings XI Punjab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kings_XI_Punjab "Kings XI Punjab") by 3 wickets with [Manish Pandey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manish_Pandey "Manish Pandey") declared the man of the match in the final. The average attendance for the tournament was 31,751.

A part of tournament was held outside India as Indian [Home Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Home_Affairs_(India) "Minister of Home Affairs (India)")[Sushil Kumar Shinde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sushilkumar_Shinde "Sushilkumar Shinde") declined to provide security for the league as the tournament took place at the same time as the [2014 Indian general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_general_election "2014 Indian general election").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-host-4) As a result, the tournament was jointly hosted by India and the [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates"). The opening 20 matches were held in the [UAE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates") at three different stadiums in [Abu Dhabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheikh_Zayed_Cricket_Stadium "Sheikh Zayed Cricket Stadium"), [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai_International_Cricket_Stadium "Dubai International Cricket Stadium") and [Sharjah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharjah_Cricket_Stadium "Sharjah Cricket Stadium") with the tournament returning to India on 2 May.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-BBCUAE-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-6)

The player auction took place on 12 and 13 February 2014. Unlike previous seasons, the auction was in [Indian Rupees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_rupee "Indian rupee") as opposed to [US dollars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar").

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2014_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

### Hosting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2014_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Hosting")]

On 14 February, BCCI secretary [Sanjay Patel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjay_Patel "Sanjay Patel") told the media after the IPL governing council meeting: "As far as possible our interest is to hold the IPL in India. Then, probably, South Africa is the preferred venue at the moment."[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The initial part of the season was held outside India, to avoid adding to the existing security demands for the [2014 Lok Sabha Elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_general_election "2014 Indian general election"). [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa"), [Bangladesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh "Bangladesh") and [UAE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates") were initially shortlisted as alternative venues.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-8) The BCCI working committee's meeting on 28 February decided that a final decision would be taken once the schedule for the general election was announced as the BCCI wanted to have as many matches as possible hosted in India due to pressure from the sponsors.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-9)

On 2 March 2014, it was reported that Sri Lanka, which was under fourth consideration for hosting the matches, had been ruled out due to prospect of rains in the country during the period.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-10) On 5 March 2014, when the dates for general elections were announced, IPL chairman [Ranjib Biswal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranjib_Biswal "Ranjib Biswal") stated that 60–70 percent of the tournament would be held in India. Also, South Africa as an alternate venue was effectively ruled out since they wanted to host the entire tournament, leaving chances open for UAE and Bangladesh.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-11)

On 12 March 2014, it was announced that the tournament would begin on 16 April and at least 16 matches would be played in [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates") until 30 April. From 1 to 12 May, BCCI approached the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India seeking permission to play IPL matches in India in cities where the polling concluded in the respective state. All matches after 12 May, which is last day of polling for the elections, would be played in India. No matches would be played on 16 May, the day for counting of votes for the general election. The final was played on 1 June 2014.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-12)

### Schedule

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2014_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Schedule")]

The schedule of the first phase of the IPL 2014 was announced on 19 March 2014.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-13) The first phase of the tournament consisted of 20 matches played from 16 to 30 April 2014 in the [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates"). The opening match of the tournament was played between the defending champions [Mumbai Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai_Indians "Mumbai Indians") and the [Kolkata Knight Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Knight_Riders "Kolkata Knight Riders") on 16 April 2014 at the [Sheikh Zayed Cricket Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheikh_Zayed_Cricket_Stadium "Sheikh Zayed Cricket Stadium") in [Abu Dhabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi "Abu Dhabi") at 6:30 pm local time (8:00 pm IST).[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-14) From 2 May onwards the 36 games of the regular season and the 4 playoffs were played in India across 10 venues.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-15)

### Insurance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2014_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Insurance")]

Since this year's IPL was played during the Lok Sabha Elections in the country, re-insurance companies asked to double the rates for insurance cover of IPL 7.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-23) The insurance cover includes parties like BCCI, franchisees and media partners. The insurance companies expected a high security danger threat during the elections period in the country. The companies demanded Rs. 140 million for a cover of Rs. 9 billion this year which is exactly double the previous year price of Rs. 70 million.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-24)

On 24 December 2013, the IPL Governing Council finalised the Player Regulations for the 2014 season.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-29) All teams were allowed to retain a maximum of five players (at most four Indian capped players) and the rest of the players had to be sent into the auction pool.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-30) Retention of players led to reduction of the teams' salary cap by a fixed amount, regardless of the players' actual salaries. Some franchises were unhappy with new retention rules.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-32) Each team had a starting salary cap of ₹ 600 million (₹ 60 crore). Three franchises retained the maximum of 5 players while [Delhi Daredevils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi_Daredevils "Delhi Daredevils") retained none.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-33)

This season's auction saw the introduction of several new rules. For the first time Indian uncapped players were also into the auction. There is no minimum quota for catchment area players restriction. All player fees was denominated in Indian rupees but overseas players may choose to be paid in another currency. There was also introduction of the "rights to match", which allowed teams to purchase a player from their 2013 squad in the auction by matching the highest bid. The number of "rights to match" depends on the number of players retained by the team.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-34) Also, the players' salaries will not include their fees for participation in the [Champions League Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_League_Twenty20 "Champions League Twenty20"). Teams who qualify will pay each player who represents them an additional 10% of his IPL fee. Previously, players who qualified for the CLT20 with their IPL team had to forfeit 20% of their IPL salary to represent another team.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-35)

On 27 January 2014 [BCCI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Control_for_Cricket_in_India "Board of Control for Cricket in India") released a list of capped players to all the franchises which would be available for the auction. This list had a total of 233 players from 10 countries. On 29 January 2014 this list was updated to 244 capped players and 651 uncapped players. On 6 February 2014, the final auction list was shortlisted by teams to 514 players (219 capped and 295 uncapped). The list was further shortened to 511 players (216 capped and 295 uncapped) after the withdrawal of 3 players.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-36) The highest base price set was of Rs 20 million and the lowest of Rs 1 million. The auction took place on 12 and 13 February.

On 7 February 2014, a plea was filed in the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_India "Supreme Court of India") to interfere in the IPL auction in relation to the [2013 Indian Premier League spot-fixing and betting case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Indian_Premier_League_spot-fixing_and_betting_case "2013 Indian Premier League spot-fixing and betting case") involving [Gurunath Meiyappan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gurunath_Meiyappan "Gurunath Meiyappan") of [Chennai Super Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai_Super_Kings "Chennai Super Kings").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-37) On 10 February 2014, an IPL spot-fixing report finding Meiyappan involved in betting was submitted to the Supreme Court.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-39) However the Supreme Court allowed the auction to go ahead as planned.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-41)

A total of 154 players including 50 overseas players were sold. The list consisted of 80 capped players (of which 34 were Indians) and 74 uncapped players. 127 players (including 10 who have only been part of the squad) have previously been part of IPL teams. 66 players will represent the same team that they played for in [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Indian_Premier_League "2013 Indian Premier League"). 13 Right to Match cards were used during the auction.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-42)[Yuvraj Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuvraj_Singh "Yuvraj Singh") fetched the highest bid of ₹14 crore (US$1.5 million) while [Dinesh Karthik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinesh_Karthik "Dinesh Karthik") was the second most expensive purchase at a price of ₹12.5 crore (US$1.3 million) by [Delhi Daredevils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi_Daredevils "Delhi Daredevils").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-43)[Kevin Pietersen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Pietersen "Kevin Pietersen") was the costliest foreign player. Among uncapped players, [Karn Sharma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karn_Sharma "Karn Sharma") was the most expensive at ₹3.75 crore (US$390,000).[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-44) Many prominent Indian players and most Sri Lankan and English players were unsold like Luke Wright & Alex Hales.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-45)

The **2014 Indian Premier League season** (abbreviated as **IPL 7** or **Pepsi IPL 2014**) was the seventh season of the [Indian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Premier_League "Indian Premier League"), a professional Twenty20 cricket league established by the [Board of Control for Cricket in India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Control_for_Cricket_in_India "Board of Control for Cricket in India") (BCCI) in 2007. The tournament featured [eight teams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League_squads "2014 Indian Premier League squads"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-1) one fewer than in 2013 after the withdrawal of the [Pune Warriors India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pune_Warriors_India "Pune Warriors India"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-3) and was held from 16 April 2014 to 1 June 2014. The opening ceremony was held in the [UAE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates") on 15 April 2014. [Kolkata Knight Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Knight_Riders "Kolkata Knight Riders") won the tournament, defeating [Kings XI Punjab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kings_XI_Punjab "Kings XI Punjab") by 3 wickets with [Manish Pandey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manish_Pandey "Manish Pandey") declared the man of the match in the final. The average attendance for the tournament was 31,751.

A part of tournament was held outside India as Indian [Home Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Home_Affairs_(India) "Minister of Home Affairs (India)")[Sushil Kumar Shinde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sushilkumar_Shinde "Sushilkumar Shinde") declined to provide security for the league as the tournament took place at the same time as the [2014 Indian general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_general_election "2014 Indian general election").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-host-4) As a result, the tournament was jointly hosted by India and the [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates"). The opening 20 matches were held in the [UAE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates") at three different stadiums in [Abu Dhabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheikh_Zayed_Cricket_Stadium "Sheikh Zayed Cricket Stadium"), [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai_International_Cricket_Stadium "Dubai International Cricket Stadium") and [Sharjah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharjah_Cricket_Stadium "Sharjah Cricket Stadium") with the tournament returning to India on 2 May.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-BBCUAE-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-6)

The player auction took place on 12 and 13 February 2014. Unlike previous seasons, the auction was in [Indian Rupees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_rupee "Indian rupee") as opposed to [US dollars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar").

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2014_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

### Hosting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2014_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Hosting")]

On 14 February, BCCI secretary [Sanjay Patel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjay_Patel "Sanjay Patel") told the media after the IPL governing council meeting: "As far as possible our interest is to hold the IPL in India. Then, probably, South Africa is the preferred venue at the moment."[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The initial part of the season was held outside India, to avoid adding to the existing security demands for the [2014 Lok Sabha Elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_general_election "2014 Indian general election"). [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa"), [Bangladesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh "Bangladesh") and [UAE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates") were initially shortlisted as alternative venues.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-8) The BCCI working committee's meeting on 28 February decided that a final decision would be taken once the schedule for the general election was announced as the BCCI wanted to have as many matches as possible hosted in India due to pressure from the sponsors.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-9)

On 2 March 2014, it was reported that Sri Lanka, which was under fourth consideration for hosting the matches, had been ruled out due to prospect of rains in the country during the period.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-10) On 5 March 2014, when the dates for general elections were announced, IPL chairman [Ranjib Biswal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranjib_Biswal "Ranjib Biswal") stated that 60–70 percent of the tournament would be held in India. Also, South Africa as an alternate venue was effectively ruled out since they wanted to host the entire tournament, leaving chances open for UAE and Bangladesh.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-11)

On 12 March 2014, it was announced that the tournament would begin on 16 April and at least 16 matches would be played in [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates") until 30 April. From 1 to 12 May, BCCI approached the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India seeking permission to play IPL matches in India in cities where the polling concluded in the respective state. All matches after 12 May, which is last day of polling for the elections, would be played in India. No matches would be played on 16 May, the day for counting of votes for the general election. The final was played on 1 June 2014.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-12)

### Schedule

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2014_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Schedule")]

The schedule of the first phase of the IPL 2014 was announced on 19 March 2014.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-13) The first phase of the tournament consisted of 20 matches played from 16 to 30 April 2014 in the [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates"). The opening match of the tournament was played between the defending champions [Mumbai Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai_Indians "Mumbai Indians") and the [Kolkata Knight Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Knight_Riders "Kolkata Knight Riders") on 16 April 2014 at the [Sheikh Zayed Cricket Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheikh_Zayed_Cricket_Stadium "Sheikh Zayed Cricket Stadium") in [Abu Dhabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi "Abu Dhabi") at 6:30 pm local time (8:00 pm IST).[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-14) From 2 May onwards the 36 games of the regular season and the 4 playoffs were played in India across 10 venues.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-15)

### Insurance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2014_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Insurance")]

Since this year's IPL was played during the Lok Sabha Elections in the country, re-insurance companies asked to double the rates for insurance cover of IPL 7.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-23) The insurance cover includes parties like BCCI, franchisees and media partners. The insurance companies expected a high security danger threat during the elections period in the country. The companies demanded Rs. 140 million for a cover of Rs. 9 billion this year which is exactly double the previous year price of Rs. 70 million.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-24)

### Broadcasting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2014_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Broadcasting")]

[Times Internet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Times_Group#Times_Internet "The Times Group") decided to share IPL digital rights with [STAR India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Star "Disney Star") giving StarSports.com streaming rights alongside [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), which had been streaming IPL since its inception in 2008.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-26) In the UK, [ITV4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV4 "ITV4") showed the league for the final time before [Sky Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_Sports "Sky Sports") took over in 2015.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ht-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-28)[Willow Cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willow_(TV_channel) "Willow (TV channel)") carried coverage of the season in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States").

On 24 December 2013, the IPL Governing Council finalised the Player Regulations for the 2014 season.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-29) All teams were allowed to retain a maximum of five players (at most four Indian capped players) and the rest of the players had to be sent into the auction pool.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-30) Retention of players led to reduction of the teams' salary cap by a fixed amount, regardless of the players' actual salaries. Some franchises were unhappy with new retention rules.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-32) Each team had a starting salary cap of ₹ 600 million (₹ 60 crore). Three franchises retained the maximum of 5 players while [Delhi Daredevils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi_Daredevils "Delhi Daredevils") retained none.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-33)

This season's auction saw the introduction of several new rules. For the first time Indian uncapped players were also into the auction. There is no minimum quota for catchment area players restriction. All player fees was denominated in Indian rupees but overseas players may choose to be paid in another currency. There was also introduction of the "rights to match", which allowed teams to purchase a player from their 2013 squad in the auction by matching the highest bid. The number of "rights to match" depends on the number of players retained by the team.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-34) Also, the players' salaries will not include their fees for participation in the [Champions League Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_League_Twenty20 "Champions League Twenty20"). Teams who qualify will pay each player who represents them an additional 10% of his IPL fee. Previously, players who qualified for the CLT20 with their IPL team had to forfeit 20% of their IPL salary to represent another team.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-35)

On 27 January 2014 [BCCI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Control_for_Cricket_in_India "Board of Control for Cricket in India") released a list of capped players to all the franchises which would be available for the auction. This list had a total of 233 players from 10 countries. On 29 January 2014 this list was updated to 244 capped players and 651 uncapped players. On 6 February 2014, the final auction list was shortlisted by teams to 514 players (219 capped and 295 uncapped). The list was further shortened to 511 players (216 capped and 295 uncapped) after the withdrawal of 3 players.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-36) The highest base price set was of Rs 20 million and the lowest of Rs 1 million. The auction took place on 12 and 13 February.

On 7 February 2014, a plea was filed in the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_India "Supreme Court of India") to interfere in the IPL auction in relation to the [2013 Indian Premier League spot-fixing and betting case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Indian_Premier_League_spot-fixing_and_betting_case "2013 Indian Premier League spot-fixing and betting case") involving [Gurunath Meiyappan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gurunath_Meiyappan "Gurunath Meiyappan") of [Chennai Super Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai_Super_Kings "Chennai Super Kings").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-37) On 10 February 2014, an IPL spot-fixing report finding Meiyappan involved in betting was submitted to the Supreme Court.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-39) However the Supreme Court allowed the auction to go ahead as planned.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-41)

A total of 154 players including 50 overseas players were sold. The list consisted of 80 capped players (of which 34 were Indians) and 74 uncapped players. 127 players (including 10 who have only been part of the squad) have previously been part of IPL teams. 66 players will represent the same team that they played for in [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Indian_Premier_League "2013 Indian Premier League"). 13 Right to Match cards were used during the auction.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-42)[Yuvraj Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuvraj_Singh "Yuvraj Singh") fetched the highest bid of ₹14 crore (US$1.5 million) while [Dinesh Karthik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinesh_Karthik "Dinesh Karthik") was the second most expensive purchase at a price of ₹12.5 crore (US$1.3 million) by [Delhi Daredevils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi_Daredevils "Delhi Daredevils").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-43)[Kevin Pietersen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Pietersen "Kevin Pietersen") was the costliest foreign player. Among uncapped players, [Karn Sharma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karn_Sharma "Karn Sharma") was the most expensive at ₹3.75 crore (US$390,000).[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-44) Many prominent Indian players and most Sri Lankan and English players were unsold like Luke Wright & Alex Hales.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-45)

The **2015 Indian Premier League season** (also known as **IPL 8** or, for sponsorship reasons, **Pepsi IPL 2015**) was the eighth season of the [Indian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Premier_League "Indian Premier League"), a [Twenty20 cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20_cricket "Twenty20 cricket") league established by the [Board of Control for Cricket in India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Control_for_Cricket_in_India "Board of Control for Cricket in India") (BCCI) in 2007. The tournament featured eight teams and was held from 8 April 2015 to 24 May 2015.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-Fixtures-1) The tournament's opening ceremony was held at the [Eden Gardens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Gardens "Eden Gardens") in [Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata "Kolkata") on 7 April 2015. [Kolkata Knight Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Knight_Riders "Kolkata Knight Riders") were the defending champions having won the title in the 2014 season.

On 24 May 2015, [Mumbai Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai_Indians "Mumbai Indians") defeated [Chennai Super Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai_Super_Kings "Chennai Super Kings") by 41 runs in the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Indian_Premier_League_final "2015 Indian Premier League final") at [Eden Gardens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Gardens "Eden Gardens"), Kolkata, to win the IPL title for the second time. Mumbai captain [Rohit Sharma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rohit_Sharma "Rohit Sharma") was awarded player of the match in the final for his knock of 50 from 26 balls. [Andre Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andre_Russell "Andre Russell") of the Kolkata Knight Riders was named Most Valuable Player (MVP) of the season. This was the last time that [Sony Television Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SONY_SIX "SONY SIX") broadcast the tournament before [Star Sports Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Sports_(Indian_TV_network) "Star Sports (Indian TV network)") took the broadcasting rights from the 8th season and are currently bearing the broadcasting rights for the tournament.

## Players auction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Players auction")]

Main article: [List of 2015 Indian Premier League personnel changes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_2015_Indian_Premier_League_personnel_changes "List of 2015 Indian Premier League personnel changes")

The eight franchises retained a total of 123 players for the 2015 IPL season before moving into the auction. The released players were provided an option to register themselves for auction. Six players were traded across teams before the auction took place. At the 2015 IPL auction held on 16 February at [Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangalore "Bangalore"), [Yuvraj Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuvraj_Singh "Yuvraj Singh") was sold to [Delhi Daredevils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi_Daredevils "Delhi Daredevils") for ₹16 crore, a record bid in IPL auction history. A total of 67 players were sold out in the auction and the franchises spent a total of ₹87.60 crore to buy the players.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-2)

## Officials

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Officials")]

The 2015 IPL season saw 26 match officials, 13 Indian umpires and four match referees officiating. 26 match officials (umpires and referees) participated in a two-day workshop, organised by the BCCI, in preparation for the 2015 IPL season. The workshop was held at the Cricket Centre, Mumbai, on 4 and 5 April 2015, from 9am to 5pm.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-3)

## IPL Fanpark initiative

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: IPL Fanpark initiative")]

BCCI started a new initiative _IPL Fanpark_ to spread the reach of IPL across the country. As a part of the initiative, IPL was made available in the stadiums across 15 cities, apart from the 12 venues hosting the matches, on a large screen. The access to these stadiums was free and based on first-come first-served basis.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-9)

## Opening ceremony

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Opening ceremony")]

The opening ceremony was held at the [Salt Lake Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_Stadium "Salt Lake Stadium") in [Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata "Kolkata"), on 7 April 2015. The captains of all eight teams signed the "MCC Spirit of Cricket" pledge. The ceremony featured live performances of [Hrithik Roshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hrithik_Roshan "Hrithik Roshan"), [Anushka Sharma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anushka_Sharma "Anushka Sharma"), [Farhan Akhtar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farhan_Akhtar "Farhan Akhtar"), [Shahid Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shahid_Kapoor "Shahid Kapoor") among others. The ceremony began after a one and a half hours delay due to rain.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-10)

The **2015 Indian Premier League season** (also known as **IPL 8** or, for sponsorship reasons, **Pepsi IPL 2015**) was the eighth season of the [Indian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Premier_League "Indian Premier League"), a [Twenty20 cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20_cricket "Twenty20 cricket") league established by the [Board of Control for Cricket in India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Control_for_Cricket_in_India "Board of Control for Cricket in India") (BCCI) in 2007. The tournament featured eight teams and was held from 8 April 2015 to 24 May 2015.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-Fixtures-1) The tournament's opening ceremony was held at the [Eden Gardens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Gardens "Eden Gardens") in [Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata "Kolkata") on 7 April 2015. [Kolkata Knight Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Knight_Riders "Kolkata Knight Riders") were the defending champions having won the title in the 2014 season.

On 24 May 2015, [Mumbai Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai_Indians "Mumbai Indians") defeated [Chennai Super Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai_Super_Kings "Chennai Super Kings") by 41 runs in the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Indian_Premier_League_final "2015 Indian Premier League final") at [Eden Gardens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Gardens "Eden Gardens"), Kolkata, to win the IPL title for the second time. Mumbai captain [Rohit Sharma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rohit_Sharma "Rohit Sharma") was awarded player of the match in the final for his knock of 50 from 26 balls. [Andre Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andre_Russell "Andre Russell") of the Kolkata Knight Riders was named Most Valuable Player (MVP) of the season. This was the last time that [Sony Television Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SONY_SIX "SONY SIX") broadcast the tournament before [Star Sports Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Sports_(Indian_TV_network) "Star Sports (Indian TV network)") took the broadcasting rights from the 8th season and are currently bearing the broadcasting rights for the tournament.

## Players auction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Players auction")]

Main article: [List of 2015 Indian Premier League personnel changes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_2015_Indian_Premier_League_personnel_changes "List of 2015 Indian Premier League personnel changes")

The eight franchises retained a total of 123 players for the 2015 IPL season before moving into the auction. The released players were provided an option to register themselves for auction. Six players were traded across teams before the auction took place. At the 2015 IPL auction held on 16 February at [Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangalore "Bangalore"), [Yuvraj Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuvraj_Singh "Yuvraj Singh") was sold to [Delhi Daredevils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi_Daredevils "Delhi Daredevils") for ₹16 crore, a record bid in IPL auction history. A total of 67 players were sold out in the auction and the franchises spent a total of ₹87.60 crore to buy the players.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-2)

## Officials

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Officials")]

The 2015 IPL season saw 26 match officials, 13 Indian umpires and four match referees officiating. 26 match officials (umpires and referees) participated in a two-day workshop, organised by the BCCI, in preparation for the 2015 IPL season. The workshop was held at the Cricket Centre, Mumbai, on 4 and 5 April 2015, from 9am to 5pm.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-3)

## IPL Fanpark initiative

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: IPL Fanpark initiative")]

BCCI started a new initiative _IPL Fanpark_ to spread the reach of IPL across the country. As a part of the initiative, IPL was made available in the stadiums across 15 cities, apart from the 12 venues hosting the matches, on a large screen. The access to these stadiums was free and based on first-come first-served basis.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-9)

## Opening ceremony

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Opening ceremony")]

The opening ceremony was held at the [Salt Lake Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_Stadium "Salt Lake Stadium") in [Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata "Kolkata"), on 7 April 2015. The captains of all eight teams signed the "MCC Spirit of Cricket" pledge. The ceremony featured live performances of [Hrithik Roshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hrithik_Roshan "Hrithik Roshan"), [Anushka Sharma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anushka_Sharma "Anushka Sharma"), [Farhan Akhtar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farhan_Akhtar "Farhan Akhtar"), [Shahid Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shahid_Kapoor "Shahid Kapoor") among others. The ceremony began after a one and a half hours delay due to rain.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-10)

The **2015 Indian Premier League season** (also known as **IPL 8** or, for sponsorship reasons, **Pepsi IPL 2015**) was the eighth season of the [Indian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Premier_League "Indian Premier League"), a [Twenty20 cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20_cricket "Twenty20 cricket") league established by the [Board of Control for Cricket in India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Control_for_Cricket_in_India "Board of Control for Cricket in India") (BCCI) in 2007. The tournament featured eight teams and was held from 8 April 2015 to 24 May 2015.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-Fixtures-1) The tournament's opening ceremony was held at the [Eden Gardens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Gardens "Eden Gardens") in [Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata "Kolkata") on 7 April 2015. [Kolkata Knight Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Knight_Riders "Kolkata Knight Riders") were the defending champions having won the title in the 2014 season.

On 24 May 2015, [Mumbai Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai_Indians "Mumbai Indians") defeated [Chennai Super Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai_Super_Kings "Chennai Super Kings") by 41 runs in the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Indian_Premier_League_final "2015 Indian Premier League final") at [Eden Gardens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Gardens "Eden Gardens"), Kolkata, to win the IPL title for the second time. Mumbai captain [Rohit Sharma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rohit_Sharma "Rohit Sharma") was awarded player of the match in the final for his knock of 50 from 26 balls. [Andre Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andre_Russell "Andre Russell") of the Kolkata Knight Riders was named Most Valuable Player (MVP) of the season. This was the last time that [Sony Television Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SONY_SIX "SONY SIX") broadcast the tournament before [Star Sports Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Sports_(Indian_TV_network) "Star Sports (Indian TV network)") took the broadcasting rights from the 8th season and are currently bearing the broadcasting rights for the tournament.

## Players auction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Players auction")]

Main article: [List of 2015 Indian Premier League personnel changes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_2015_Indian_Premier_League_personnel_changes "List of 2015 Indian Premier League personnel changes")

The eight franchises retained a total of 123 players for the 2015 IPL season before moving into the auction. The released players were provided an option to register themselves for auction. Six players were traded across teams before the auction took place. At the 2015 IPL auction held on 16 February at [Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangalore "Bangalore"), [Yuvraj Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuvraj_Singh "Yuvraj Singh") was sold to [Delhi Daredevils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi_Daredevils "Delhi Daredevils") for ₹16 crore, a record bid in IPL auction history. A total of 67 players were sold out in the auction and the franchises spent a total of ₹87.60 crore to buy the players.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-2)

## Officials

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Officials")]

The 2015 IPL season saw 26 match officials, 13 Indian umpires and four match referees officiating. 26 match officials (umpires and referees) participated in a two-day workshop, organised by the BCCI, in preparation for the 2015 IPL season. The workshop was held at the Cricket Centre, Mumbai, on 4 and 5 April 2015, from 9am to 5pm.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-3)

## IPL Fanpark initiative

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: IPL Fanpark initiative")]

BCCI started a new initiative _IPL Fanpark_ to spread the reach of IPL across the country. As a part of the initiative, IPL was made available in the stadiums across 15 cities, apart from the 12 venues hosting the matches, on a large screen. The access to these stadiums was free and based on first-come first-served basis.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-9)

## Opening ceremony

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Opening ceremony")]

The opening ceremony was held at the [Salt Lake Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_Stadium "Salt Lake Stadium") in [Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata "Kolkata"), on 7 April 2015. The captains of all eight teams signed the "MCC Spirit of Cricket" pledge. The ceremony featured live performances of [Hrithik Roshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hrithik_Roshan "Hrithik Roshan"), [Anushka Sharma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anushka_Sharma "Anushka Sharma"), [Farhan Akhtar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farhan_Akhtar "Farhan Akhtar"), [Shahid Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shahid_Kapoor "Shahid Kapoor") among others. The ceremony began after a one and a half hours delay due to rain.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-10)

The **Bangladesh Premier League 2016**, also known as **BPL Season 4** and **AKS BPL 2016** (for sponsorship reasons) was the fourth season of the [Bangladesh Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh_Premier_League "Bangladesh Premier League") (BPL), the top level professional [Twenty20 cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20_cricket "Twenty20 cricket") franchise league in Bangladesh. The competition was organised by the [Bangladesh Cricket Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh_Cricket_Board "Bangladesh Cricket Board") (BCB) and featured seven teams.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci10sep16-1) The season originally began on 4 November 2016 and ended on 9 December 2016.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci4nov16-2) However, after the first four matches of the tournament were abandoned due to rain and with more rain forecast, the league opted to restart on 8 November and to replay all six of the opening six matches.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci4nov16-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci5nov16-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-replay-4)

Two new teams, [Khulna Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khulna_Titans "Khulna Titans") and [Rajshahi Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajshahi_Kings "Rajshahi Kings") played in the competition under new owners after the original franchisees were not allowed to enter the [2015 competition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Bangladesh_Premier_League "2015 Bangladesh Premier League"), while the [Sylhet Super Stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylhet_Super_Stars "Sylhet Super Stars") franchise was excluded from the competition.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci10sep16-1)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci21sep16-5) The BCB originally claimed that Sylhet had breached franchisee agreements or not paid bank guarantees, but on 21 September clarified that the franchise had been excluded for "disciplinary reasons".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci21sep16-5)[Comilla Victorians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comilla_Victorians "Comilla Victorians") were the defending champions[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-defending-6) but were eliminated in the group stage. In the championship game, [Dhaka Dynamites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhaka_Dynamites "Dhaka Dynamites") defeated Rajshahi Kings to win their third title.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-champs-7)

## Draft and Squads

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016%E2%80%9317_Bangladesh_Premier_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Draft and Squads")]

The 2016 BPL draft was held on 30 September.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci10sep16-1)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-DT-Fran-8) Prior to the draft, the seven clubs signed 38 foreign players to contracts and each existing franchise was able to retain two home-grown players from the 2015 season.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-DT-Gayle-9) A total 301 players participated in the draft, including 133 local and 168 foreign players. 85 players were selected in the draft.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-85draft-10)

### Player transfers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016%E2%80%9317_Bangladesh_Premier_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Player transfers")]

Prior to the 2016 draft, a number of high-profile players moved teams. These included transfers between competing teams and due to the suspension of the [Sylhet Super Stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylhet_Super_Stars "Sylhet Super Stars") and the introduction of two new teams, [Khulna Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khulna_Titans "Khulna Titans") and [Rajshahi Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajshahi_Kings "Rajshahi Kings"). Transfers included the move of [Barisal Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barisal_Bulls "Barisal Bulls") captain [Mahmudullah Riyad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahmudullah_Riyad "Mahmudullah Riyad") to the Khulna Titans, [Chris Gayle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Gayle "Chris Gayle") from the Barisal Bulls to the [Chittagong Vikings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chittagong_Vikings "Chittagong Vikings"), the signing of [Shahid Afridi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shahid_Afridi "Shahid Afridi") as team captain of [Rangpur Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangpur_Riders "Rangpur Riders") from the Sylhet Super Stars and [Shakib Al Hasan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakib_Al_Hasan "Shakib Al Hasan") as team captain of [Dhaka Dynamites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhaka_Dynamites "Dhaka Dynamites") from Rangpur Riders.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-Gayle-11)

## League stage

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016%E2%80%9317_Bangladesh_Premier_League&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: League stage")]

A total of 46 matches were played in the tournament. During the round-robin group stage each team played 12 matches, two against each other team taking part in the tournament. In total 42 matches were played in the group stage, with the top four teams progressing to the playoff stage of the tournament where three playoff matches and the final were played, the final taking place on 9 December at the [Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sher-e-Bangla_National_Cricket_Stadium "Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium") in [Dhaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhaka "Dhaka").

Group stage matches were played in three blocks. The first and third blocks took place in Dhaka, with the middle block of 10 matches taking place in [Chittagong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chittagong "Chittagong"). Two matches were played on each day of the group stage part of the tournament. The first four matches of the tournament were washed out after heavy rain,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci4nov16-2) and the two matches scheduled to take place on 6 November were postponed.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci5nov16-3) The tournament was restarted on 8 November with the first six fixtures rescheduled[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci5nov16-3) and the matches from the opening day of fixtures replayed, with the points table reset.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-replay-4)

The **Bangladesh Premier League 2016**, also known as **BPL Season 4** and **AKS BPL 2016** (for sponsorship reasons) was the fourth season of the [Bangladesh Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh_Premier_League "Bangladesh Premier League") (BPL), the top level professional [Twenty20 cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20_cricket "Twenty20 cricket") franchise league in Bangladesh. The competition was organised by the [Bangladesh Cricket Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh_Cricket_Board "Bangladesh Cricket Board") (BCB) and featured seven teams.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci10sep16-1) The season originally began on 4 November 2016 and ended on 9 December 2016.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci4nov16-2) However, after the first four matches of the tournament were abandoned due to rain and with more rain forecast, the league opted to restart on 8 November and to replay all six of the opening six matches.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci4nov16-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci5nov16-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-replay-4)

Two new teams, [Khulna Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khulna_Titans "Khulna Titans") and [Rajshahi Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajshahi_Kings "Rajshahi Kings") played in the competition under new owners after the original franchisees were not allowed to enter the [2015 competition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Bangladesh_Premier_League "2015 Bangladesh Premier League"), while the [Sylhet Super Stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylhet_Super_Stars "Sylhet Super Stars") franchise was excluded from the competition.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci10sep16-1)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci21sep16-5) The BCB originally claimed that Sylhet had breached franchisee agreements or not paid bank guarantees, but on 21 September clarified that the franchise had been excluded for "disciplinary reasons".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci21sep16-5)[Comilla Victorians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comilla_Victorians "Comilla Victorians") were the defending champions[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-defending-6) but were eliminated in the group stage. In the championship game, [Dhaka Dynamites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhaka_Dynamites "Dhaka Dynamites") defeated Rajshahi Kings to win their third title.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-champs-7)

## Draft and Squads

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016%E2%80%9317_Bangladesh_Premier_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Draft and Squads")]

The 2016 BPL draft was held on 30 September.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci10sep16-1)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-DT-Fran-8) Prior to the draft, the seven clubs signed 38 foreign players to contracts and each existing franchise was able to retain two home-grown players from the 2015 season.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-DT-Gayle-9) A total 301 players participated in the draft, including 133 local and 168 foreign players. 85 players were selected in the draft.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-85draft-10)

### Player transfers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016%E2%80%9317_Bangladesh_Premier_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Player transfers")]

Prior to the 2016 draft, a number of high-profile players moved teams. These included transfers between competing teams and due to the suspension of the [Sylhet Super Stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylhet_Super_Stars "Sylhet Super Stars") and the introduction of two new teams, [Khulna Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khulna_Titans "Khulna Titans") and [Rajshahi Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajshahi_Kings "Rajshahi Kings"). Transfers included the move of [Barisal Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barisal_Bulls "Barisal Bulls") captain [Mahmudullah Riyad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahmudullah_Riyad "Mahmudullah Riyad") to the Khulna Titans, [Chris Gayle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Gayle "Chris Gayle") from the Barisal Bulls to the [Chittagong Vikings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chittagong_Vikings "Chittagong Vikings"), the signing of [Shahid Afridi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shahid_Afridi "Shahid Afridi") as team captain of [Rangpur Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangpur_Riders "Rangpur Riders") from the Sylhet Super Stars and [Shakib Al Hasan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakib_Al_Hasan "Shakib Al Hasan") as team captain of [Dhaka Dynamites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhaka_Dynamites "Dhaka Dynamites") from Rangpur Riders.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-Gayle-11)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016%E2%80%9317_Bangladesh_Premier_League&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Venues")]

## League stage

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016%E2%80%9317_Bangladesh_Premier_League&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: League stage")]

A total of 46 matches were played in the tournament. During the round-robin group stage each team played 12 matches, two against each other team taking part in the tournament. In total 42 matches were played in the group stage, with the top four teams progressing to the playoff stage of the tournament where three playoff matches and the final were played, the final taking place on 9 December at the [Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sher-e-Bangla_National_Cricket_Stadium "Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium") in [Dhaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhaka "Dhaka").

Group stage matches were played in three blocks. The first and third blocks took place in Dhaka, with the middle block of 10 matches taking place in [Chittagong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chittagong "Chittagong"). Two matches were played on each day of the group stage part of the tournament. The first four matches of the tournament were washed out after heavy rain,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci4nov16-2) and the two matches scheduled to take place on 6 November were postponed.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci5nov16-3) The tournament was restarted on 8 November with the first six fixtures rescheduled[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-ci5nov16-3) and the matches from the opening day of fixtures replayed, with the points table reset.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bangladesh_Premier_League#cite_note-replay-4)

The **2016 Indian Premier League season** (also known as **IPL 9**, and branded as **Vivo IPL 2016** for sponsorship reasons) was the ninth season of the [Indian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Premier_League "Indian Premier League"), a professional [Twenty20 cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20_cricket "Twenty20 cricket") league established by the [Board of Control for Cricket in India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Control_for_Cricket_in_India "Board of Control for Cricket in India") (BCCI) in 2007. The season began on 9 April 2016 and concluded on 29 May 2016 with the playing of the finals match between [Royal Challengers Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Challengers_Bangalore "Royal Challengers Bangalore") and [Sunrisers Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunrisers_Hyderabad "Sunrisers Hyderabad") at [M. Chinnaswamy Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M._Chinnaswamy_Stadium "M. Chinnaswamy Stadium") in [Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangalore "Bangalore").

The 2016 season was the first IPL season to use LED [stumps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stump_(cricket) "Stump (cricket)"). Following the suspension of [Chennai Super Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai_Super_Kings "Chennai Super Kings") and [Rajasthan Royals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajasthan_Royals "Rajasthan Royals") for two years over a [spot-fixing and betting case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Indian_Premier_League_spot-fixing_and_betting_case "2013 Indian Premier League spot-fixing and betting case") during the 2013 IPL season, the IPL allocated spots for two new franchises to take their place. The process would result in the establishment of the [Gujarat Lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat_Lions "Gujarat Lions") and [Rising Pune Supergiants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rising_Pune_Supergiants "Rising Pune Supergiants").

The championship was won by [Sunrisers Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunrisers_Hyderabad "Sunrisers Hyderabad"), marking the [Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyderabad "Hyderabad") franchise's second IPL title, with [Ben Cutting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Cutting "Ben Cutting") declared the man of the match in the final. [Virat Kohli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virat_Kohli "Virat Kohli") of [Royal Challengers Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Challengers_Bangalore "Royal Challengers Bangalore") was named the most valuable player of the tournament, and [Mustafizur Rahman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mustafizur_Rahman "Mustafizur Rahman") of Sunrisers Hyderabad was named the emerging player of the season. Kohli was the tournament's leading run-scorer with 973 runs and [Bhuvneshwar Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuvneshwar_Kumar "Bhuvneshwar Kumar") of [Sunrisers Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunrisers_Hyderabad "Sunrisers Hyderabad") was the leading wicket-taker of the tournament with 23 wickets. Ever since the introduction of [Page playoff system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Page_playoff_system "Page playoff system"), this is the only edition where a team ending outside of the top 2 at the end of league stage won an IPL title.

## Format

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Format")]

Eight teams contested the season. Two teams, [Rising Pune Supergiants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rising_Pune_Supergiants "Rising Pune Supergiants") and [Gujarat Lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat_Lions "Gujarat Lions"), based in [Pune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pune "Pune") and [Rajkot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajkot "Rajkot") were new to the tournament, replacing the [Chennai Super Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai_Super_Kings "Chennai Super Kings") and [Rajasthan Royals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajasthan_Royals "Rajasthan Royals") franchises which had been suspended until 2018.

The schedule for the tournament was published on 10 March 2016. The league stage, consisting of 56 matches, took place between 9 April and 22 May 2016. The top four teams qualified for the play-off stage, with the final being held in [Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangalore "Bangalore") on 29 May.

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Background")]

On 14 July 2015, the RM Lodha committee suspended the owners of the [Chennai Super Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai_Super_Kings "Chennai Super Kings") and [Rajasthan Royals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajasthan_Royals "Rajasthan Royals") franchises for a period of two years on charges of [spot-fixing and betting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Indian_Premier_League_spot-fixing_and_betting_case "2013 Indian Premier League spot-fixing and betting case") during the 2013 IPL season. This meant that the two teams could not play in the 2016 and 2017 IPL seasons.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-1) The [Board of Control of Cricket in India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Control_of_Cricket_in_India "Board of Control of Cricket in India") (BCCI) confirmed that two new teams will replace them for the next two seasons of the IPL.

In October 2015, [PepsiCo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PepsiCo "PepsiCo") withdrew as the title sponsor of the IPL, terminating a five-year deal which was to end in 2017. Chinese smartphone manufacturer [Vivo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivo_(smartphone) "Vivo (smartphone)") was awarded the title sponsorship for the 2016 and 2017 seasons.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-2)

In November 2015, the BCCI shortlisted nine cities for the new franchises to be based in, leaving out [Jaipur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaipur "Jaipur") (home of Rajasthan Royals) and [Kochi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kochi "Kochi") (home of the now defunct [Kochi Tuskers Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kochi_Tuskers_Kerala "Kochi Tuskers Kerala")) for unknown reasons.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-dec8-3) The nine cities shortlisted were: [Chennai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai "Chennai"), [Cuttack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuttack "Cuttack"), [Dharamshala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharamshala "Dharamshala"), [Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore"), [Nagpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagpur "Nagpur"), [Pune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pune "Pune"), [Rajkot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajkot "Rajkot"), [Ranchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranchi "Ranchi") and [Visakhapatnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visakhapatnam "Visakhapatnam").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-4) The new franchises were allocated using a reverse auction process, with companies which bid the lowest share of the central revenue pool becoming the owners of the new teams.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-dec8-3) On 3 December, it was reported that twelve companies collected tender documents for the bidding process.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-eco-5)

On 8 December 2015, it was announced that New Rising, a company led by [Sanjiv Goenka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjiv_Goenka "Sanjiv Goenka"), and [Intex Technologies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intex_Technologies "Intex Technologies") had won the bidding rights to the two new teams. New Rising decided to have their team based in [Pune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rising_Pune_Supergiants "Rising Pune Supergiants") while Intex chose [Rajkot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat_Lions "Gujarat Lions") as the home of its team.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-Teams_Announced-6) The two franchises picked five players each from the squads of Chennai Super Kings and Rajasthan Royals at a player draft on 15 December 2015. Each franchise was allocated a purse of ₹660 million to buy the players for their squad at the draft and players auction.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-eco-5)

### Maharashtra water crisis

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Maharashtra water crisis")]

On 6 April 2016, amid a severe drought situation in the state of [Maharashtra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharashtra "Maharashtra"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ciwater6apr16-7) in which three venues (Mumbai, Pune and Nagpur) were supposed to host a total of 20 IPL matches in the 2016 season, the [Bombay High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay_High_Court "Bombay High Court") questioned the "criminal wastage"[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-toiwater9apr16-8) of water being supplied to the three stadiums in a response to a petition from the [Lok Satta Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Satta_Movement "Lok Satta Movement") NGO.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-hindu7apr16-9) The drought was described as one of the "worst-ever droughts" to affect the state[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ciwater6apr16-7) and was believed to be one of the worst droughts in 100 years.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-bbc13apr16-10) An estimated 6 million litres (6 million litres)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-bbc13apr16-10) of water were to be used at the three venues to maintain the pitches, with 4 million litres being used at the [Wankhede Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wankhede_Stadium "Wankhede Stadium"), the site of eight matches.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-hindu7apr16-9)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-mmwater9apr16-11) The High Court filed a [public interest litigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_interest_litigation "Public interest litigation") and suggested shifting matches to "some other state where water is in abundance." The High Court questioned the [BCCI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Control_for_Cricket_in_India "Board of Control for Cricket in India") about whether "people are more important or your IPL matches".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-mmwater9apr16-11) The BCCI argued that the water being used at the venues was tanker water and not drinkable.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ciwater6apr16-7)

On 8 April, the Chief Minister of Maharashtra [Devendra Fadnavis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devendra_Fadnavis "Devendra Fadnavis") declared that potable water will not be supplied to the venues and added "even if IPL matches are shifted, we have no problem."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-toiwater9apr16-8) On 9 April, hours before the season's opening match, the [Mumbai Cricket Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai_Cricket_Association "Mumbai Cricket Association") claimed that the water being used at the Wankhede Stadium was bought from private operators and not [Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brihanmumbai_Municipal_Corporation "Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-tiewater9apr16-12)

On 13 April, the Bombay High Court ruled that all the matches to be held in the state in May must be moved to venues outside of Maharashtra. A total of 13 matches were scheduled to be hosted by the three venues in Maharashtra in the month of May, including two playoff matches in Pune and the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League_final "2016 Indian Premier League final") in Mumbai.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-bbc13apr16-10)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-moved-14) The court later allowed a match scheduled for 1 May to take place in Pune due to logistical difficulties with moving the fixture.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ci20apr16-15)

The Mumbai Cricket Association and the [Maharashtra Cricket Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharashtra_Cricket_Association "Maharashtra Cricket Association") petitioned the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_(India) "Supreme Court (India)") against the High Court's ruling, filing a plea which stated that treated sewage water will be used instead of potable water.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-mca-16) After the [Mumbai Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai_Indians "Mumbai Indians") selected [Jaipur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaipur "Jaipur") as their alternative venue, a petition was filed in the city which stated hosting IPL matches "will add unnecessary burden on the scarce natural resource."[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-17) The [Rajasthan High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajasthan_High_Court "Rajasthan High Court") then questioned the state government and BCCI about shifting the matches to [Rajasthan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajasthan "Rajasthan"), a region also hit by drought, scheduling the hearing for 27 April.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-18) There were reports of protests being held in Jaipur against the shifting of matches to the city.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-mca-16)

On 26 April the Supreme Court dismissed the petition against the Bombay High Court's ruling and confirmed that matches should be moved out of Maharashtra.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ie27apr16-19) The court had initially suggested that a series of regulations could be used to allow matches to go ahead under the condition that no drinkable water was used on the grounds, but opted to instead move the matches on the grounds that the suggested regulations would be complex and difficult to enforce.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ie27apr16-19)

On 29 April, it was announced that all league stage matches scheduled to be held after 1 May in Mumbai and Pune were shifted to the [Dr. Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy ACA-VDCA Cricket Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Y.S._Rajasekhara_Reddy_ACA-VDCA_Cricket_Stadium "Dr. Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy ACA-VDCA Cricket Stadium") in [Visakhapatnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visakhapatnam "Visakhapatnam"). Two playoff matches scheduled to be held in Pune were shifted to Delhi and three [Kings XI Punjab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kings_XI_Punjab "Kings XI Punjab") home matches supposed to be held in Nagpur were shifted to their primary home venue, Mohali. The [M. Chinnaswamy Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M._Chinnaswamy_Stadium "M. Chinnaswamy Stadium") in Bangalore, which was scheduled to host the Qualifier 1, was also announced as the host of the Final.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-vizag-20)

## Opening ceremony

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Opening ceremony")]

The opening ceremony was held on 8 April 2016 from 19:30 IST at the [Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sardar_Vallabhbhai_Patel_Indoor_Stadium "Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Indoor Stadium") in Mumbai. It featured performances from [Major Lazer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_Lazer "Major Lazer"), [Yo Yo Honey Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yo_Yo_Honey_Singh "Yo Yo Honey Singh"), [Ranveer Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranveer_Singh "Ranveer Singh"), [Katrina Kaif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katrina_Kaif "Katrina Kaif"), [Jacqueline Fernandez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacqueline_Fernandez "Jacqueline Fernandez") among others.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-21)[Dwayne Bravo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwayne_Bravo "Dwayne Bravo"), a member of the West Indies' [2016 World Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_World_Twenty20 "2016 World Twenty20") winning team, performed the "Champion Dance", which, according to the IPL chairman [Rajeev Shukla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajeev_Shukla "Rajeev Shukla"), was supposed to be the "special attraction" of the ceremony.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ie-22)

Venues used during the season

Ten venues were selected to host the league stage matches.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-23)[Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangalore "Bangalore") hosted Qualifier 1, [Pune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pune "Pune") was scheduled to host the Eliminator match and Qualifier 2 and [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai") was scheduled to host the final.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-24) The drought situation in [Maharashtra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharashtra "Maharashtra") led to a ruling in the [Bombay High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay_High_Court "Bombay High Court") that games to be played in the state, including in Pune and Mumbai, in May would have to be moved to other regions to allow water supplies to be prioritised.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-bbc13apr16-10) On 29 April 2016, the IPL Governing Council announced that all homes games of the Mumbai Indians and Rising Pune Supergiants after 2 May 2016, would be held at [Visakhapatnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visakhapatnam "Visakhapatnam"). The Eliminator and Qualifier 2 would to be held at [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi"), and the final at [Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangalore "Bangalore").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-vizag-20) On 2 May 2016, it was announced that Gujarat Lions would play two of their matches on 19 and 21 May at [Kanpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanpur "Kanpur").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-25)

## Personnel changes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personnel changes")]

Main article: [List of 2016 Indian Premier League personnel changes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_2016_Indian_Premier_League_personnel_changes "List of 2016 Indian Premier League personnel changes")

Each franchise was able to retain players from the previous season of the tournament, with their salaries automatically deducted from the franchise's available salary purse. The new teams were able to draft five players each from the two suspended franchises. Players were able to be traded during the trading windows and new players could be added to the teams at the 2016 IPL players auction held on 6 February 2016.
