The **2016 Indian Premier League season** (also known as **IPL 9**, and branded as **Vivo IPL 2016** for sponsorship reasons) was the ninth season of the [Indian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Premier_League "Indian Premier League"), a professional [Twenty20 cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20_cricket "Twenty20 cricket") league established by the [Board of Control for Cricket in India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Control_for_Cricket_in_India "Board of Control for Cricket in India") (BCCI) in 2007. The season began on 9 April 2016 and concluded on 29 May 2016 with the playing of the finals match between [Royal Challengers Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Challengers_Bangalore "Royal Challengers Bangalore") and [Sunrisers Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunrisers_Hyderabad "Sunrisers Hyderabad") at [M. Chinnaswamy Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M._Chinnaswamy_Stadium "M. Chinnaswamy Stadium") in [Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangalore "Bangalore").

The 2016 season was the first IPL season to use LED [stumps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stump_(cricket) "Stump (cricket)"). Following the suspension of [Chennai Super Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai_Super_Kings "Chennai Super Kings") and [Rajasthan Royals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajasthan_Royals "Rajasthan Royals") for two years over a [spot-fixing and betting case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Indian_Premier_League_spot-fixing_and_betting_case "2013 Indian Premier League spot-fixing and betting case") during the 2013 IPL season, the IPL allocated spots for two new franchises to take their place. The process would result in the establishment of the [Gujarat Lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat_Lions "Gujarat Lions") and [Rising Pune Supergiants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rising_Pune_Supergiants "Rising Pune Supergiants").

The championship was won by [Sunrisers Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunrisers_Hyderabad "Sunrisers Hyderabad"), marking the [Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyderabad "Hyderabad") franchise's second IPL title, with [Ben Cutting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Cutting "Ben Cutting") declared the man of the match in the final. [Virat Kohli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virat_Kohli "Virat Kohli") of [Royal Challengers Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Challengers_Bangalore "Royal Challengers Bangalore") was named the most valuable player of the tournament, and [Mustafizur Rahman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mustafizur_Rahman "Mustafizur Rahman") of Sunrisers Hyderabad was named the emerging player of the season. Kohli was the tournament's leading run-scorer with 973 runs and [Bhuvneshwar Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuvneshwar_Kumar "Bhuvneshwar Kumar") of [Sunrisers Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunrisers_Hyderabad "Sunrisers Hyderabad") was the leading wicket-taker of the tournament with 23 wickets. Ever since the introduction of [Page playoff system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Page_playoff_system "Page playoff system"), this is the only edition where a team ending outside of the top 2 at the end of league stage won an IPL title.

## Format

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Format")]

Eight teams contested the season. Two teams, [Rising Pune Supergiants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rising_Pune_Supergiants "Rising Pune Supergiants") and [Gujarat Lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat_Lions "Gujarat Lions"), based in [Pune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pune "Pune") and [Rajkot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajkot "Rajkot") were new to the tournament, replacing the [Chennai Super Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai_Super_Kings "Chennai Super Kings") and [Rajasthan Royals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajasthan_Royals "Rajasthan Royals") franchises which had been suspended until 2018.

The schedule for the tournament was published on 10 March 2016. The league stage, consisting of 56 matches, took place between 9 April and 22 May 2016. The top four teams qualified for the play-off stage, with the final being held in [Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangalore "Bangalore") on 29 May.

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Background")]

On 14 July 2015, the RM Lodha committee suspended the owners of the [Chennai Super Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai_Super_Kings "Chennai Super Kings") and [Rajasthan Royals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajasthan_Royals "Rajasthan Royals") franchises for a period of two years on charges of [spot-fixing and betting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Indian_Premier_League_spot-fixing_and_betting_case "2013 Indian Premier League spot-fixing and betting case") during the 2013 IPL season. This meant that the two teams could not play in the 2016 and 2017 IPL seasons.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-1) The [Board of Control of Cricket in India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Control_of_Cricket_in_India "Board of Control of Cricket in India") (BCCI) confirmed that two new teams will replace them for the next two seasons of the IPL.

In October 2015, [PepsiCo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PepsiCo "PepsiCo") withdrew as the title sponsor of the IPL, terminating a five-year deal which was to end in 2017. Chinese smartphone manufacturer [Vivo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivo_(smartphone) "Vivo (smartphone)") was awarded the title sponsorship for the 2016 and 2017 seasons.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-2)

In November 2015, the BCCI shortlisted nine cities for the new franchises to be based in, leaving out [Jaipur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaipur "Jaipur") (home of Rajasthan Royals) and [Kochi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kochi "Kochi") (home of the now defunct [Kochi Tuskers Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kochi_Tuskers_Kerala "Kochi Tuskers Kerala")) for unknown reasons.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-dec8-3) The nine cities shortlisted were: [Chennai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai "Chennai"), [Cuttack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuttack "Cuttack"), [Dharamshala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharamshala "Dharamshala"), [Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore"), [Nagpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagpur "Nagpur"), [Pune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pune "Pune"), [Rajkot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajkot "Rajkot"), [Ranchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranchi "Ranchi") and [Visakhapatnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visakhapatnam "Visakhapatnam").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-4) The new franchises were allocated using a reverse auction process, with companies which bid the lowest share of the central revenue pool becoming the owners of the new teams.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-dec8-3) On 3 December, it was reported that twelve companies collected tender documents for the bidding process.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-eco-5)

On 8 December 2015, it was announced that New Rising, a company led by [Sanjiv Goenka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjiv_Goenka "Sanjiv Goenka"), and [Intex Technologies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intex_Technologies "Intex Technologies") had won the bidding rights to the two new teams. New Rising decided to have their team based in [Pune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rising_Pune_Supergiants "Rising Pune Supergiants") while Intex chose [Rajkot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat_Lions "Gujarat Lions") as the home of its team.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-Teams_Announced-6) The two franchises picked five players each from the squads of Chennai Super Kings and Rajasthan Royals at a player draft on 15 December 2015. Each franchise was allocated a purse of ₹660 million to buy the players for their squad at the draft and players auction.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-eco-5)

### Maharashtra water crisis

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Maharashtra water crisis")]

On 6 April 2016, amid a severe drought situation in the state of [Maharashtra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharashtra "Maharashtra"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ciwater6apr16-7) in which three venues (Mumbai, Pune and Nagpur) were supposed to host a total of 20 IPL matches in the 2016 season, the [Bombay High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay_High_Court "Bombay High Court") questioned the "criminal wastage"[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-toiwater9apr16-8) of water being supplied to the three stadiums in a response to a petition from the [Lok Satta Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Satta_Movement "Lok Satta Movement") NGO.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-hindu7apr16-9) The drought was described as one of the "worst-ever droughts" to affect the state[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ciwater6apr16-7) and was believed to be one of the worst droughts in 100 years.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-bbc13apr16-10) An estimated 6 million litres (6 million litres)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-bbc13apr16-10) of water were to be used at the three venues to maintain the pitches, with 4 million litres being used at the [Wankhede Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wankhede_Stadium "Wankhede Stadium"), the site of eight matches.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-hindu7apr16-9)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-mmwater9apr16-11) The High Court filed a [public interest litigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_interest_litigation "Public interest litigation") and suggested shifting matches to "some other state where water is in abundance." The High Court questioned the [BCCI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Control_for_Cricket_in_India "Board of Control for Cricket in India") about whether "people are more important or your IPL matches".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-mmwater9apr16-11) The BCCI argued that the water being used at the venues was tanker water and not drinkable.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ciwater6apr16-7)

On 8 April, the Chief Minister of Maharashtra [Devendra Fadnavis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devendra_Fadnavis "Devendra Fadnavis") declared that potable water will not be supplied to the venues and added "even if IPL matches are shifted, we have no problem."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-toiwater9apr16-8) On 9 April, hours before the season's opening match, the [Mumbai Cricket Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai_Cricket_Association "Mumbai Cricket Association") claimed that the water being used at the Wankhede Stadium was bought from private operators and not [Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brihanmumbai_Municipal_Corporation "Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-tiewater9apr16-12)

On 13 April, the Bombay High Court ruled that all the matches to be held in the state in May must be moved to venues outside of Maharashtra. A total of 13 matches were scheduled to be hosted by the three venues in Maharashtra in the month of May, including two playoff matches in Pune and the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League_final "2016 Indian Premier League final") in Mumbai.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-bbc13apr16-10)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-moved-14) The court later allowed a match scheduled for 1 May to take place in Pune due to logistical difficulties with moving the fixture.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ci20apr16-15)

The Mumbai Cricket Association and the [Maharashtra Cricket Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharashtra_Cricket_Association "Maharashtra Cricket Association") petitioned the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_(India) "Supreme Court (India)") against the High Court's ruling, filing a plea which stated that treated sewage water will be used instead of potable water.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-mca-16) After the [Mumbai Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai_Indians "Mumbai Indians") selected [Jaipur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaipur "Jaipur") as their alternative venue, a petition was filed in the city which stated hosting IPL matches "will add unnecessary burden on the scarce natural resource."[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-17) The [Rajasthan High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajasthan_High_Court "Rajasthan High Court") then questioned the state government and BCCI about shifting the matches to [Rajasthan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajasthan "Rajasthan"), a region also hit by drought, scheduling the hearing for 27 April.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-18) There were reports of protests being held in Jaipur against the shifting of matches to the city.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-mca-16)

On 26 April the Supreme Court dismissed the petition against the Bombay High Court's ruling and confirmed that matches should be moved out of Maharashtra.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ie27apr16-19) The court had initially suggested that a series of regulations could be used to allow matches to go ahead under the condition that no drinkable water was used on the grounds, but opted to instead move the matches on the grounds that the suggested regulations would be complex and difficult to enforce.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ie27apr16-19)

On 29 April, it was announced that all league stage matches scheduled to be held after 1 May in Mumbai and Pune were shifted to the [Dr. Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy ACA-VDCA Cricket Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Y.S._Rajasekhara_Reddy_ACA-VDCA_Cricket_Stadium "Dr. Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy ACA-VDCA Cricket Stadium") in [Visakhapatnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visakhapatnam "Visakhapatnam"). Two playoff matches scheduled to be held in Pune were shifted to Delhi and three [Kings XI Punjab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kings_XI_Punjab "Kings XI Punjab") home matches supposed to be held in Nagpur were shifted to their primary home venue, Mohali. The [M. Chinnaswamy Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M._Chinnaswamy_Stadium "M. Chinnaswamy Stadium") in Bangalore, which was scheduled to host the Qualifier 1, was also announced as the host of the Final.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-vizag-20)

## Opening ceremony

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Opening ceremony")]

The opening ceremony was held on 8 April 2016 from 19:30 IST at the [Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sardar_Vallabhbhai_Patel_Indoor_Stadium "Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Indoor Stadium") in Mumbai. It featured performances from [Major Lazer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_Lazer "Major Lazer"), [Yo Yo Honey Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yo_Yo_Honey_Singh "Yo Yo Honey Singh"), [Ranveer Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranveer_Singh "Ranveer Singh"), [Katrina Kaif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katrina_Kaif "Katrina Kaif"), [Jacqueline Fernandez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacqueline_Fernandez "Jacqueline Fernandez") among others.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-21)[Dwayne Bravo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwayne_Bravo "Dwayne Bravo"), a member of the West Indies' [2016 World Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_World_Twenty20 "2016 World Twenty20") winning team, performed the "Champion Dance", which, according to the IPL chairman [Rajeev Shukla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajeev_Shukla "Rajeev Shukla"), was supposed to be the "special attraction" of the ceremony.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ie-22)

Ten venues were selected to host the league stage matches.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-23)[Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangalore "Bangalore") hosted Qualifier 1, [Pune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pune "Pune") was scheduled to host the Eliminator match and Qualifier 2 and [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai") was scheduled to host the final.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-24) The drought situation in [Maharashtra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharashtra "Maharashtra") led to a ruling in the [Bombay High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay_High_Court "Bombay High Court") that games to be played in the state, including in Pune and Mumbai, in May would have to be moved to other regions to allow water supplies to be prioritised.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-bbc13apr16-10) On 29 April 2016, the IPL Governing Council announced that all homes games of the Mumbai Indians and Rising Pune Supergiants after 2 May 2016, would be held at [Visakhapatnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visakhapatnam "Visakhapatnam"). The Eliminator and Qualifier 2 would to be held at [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi"), and the final at [Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangalore "Bangalore").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-vizag-20) On 2 May 2016, it was announced that Gujarat Lions would play two of their matches on 19 and 21 May at [Kanpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanpur "Kanpur").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-25)

## Personnel changes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personnel changes")]

Main article: [List of 2016 Indian Premier League personnel changes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_2016_Indian_Premier_League_personnel_changes "List of 2016 Indian Premier League personnel changes")

Each franchise was able to retain players from the previous season of the tournament, with their salaries automatically deducted from the franchise's available salary purse. The new teams were able to draft five players each from the two suspended franchises. Players were able to be traded during the trading windows and new players could be added to the teams at the 2016 IPL players auction held on 6 February 2016.

The **2016 Indian Premier League season** (also known as **IPL 9**, and branded as **Vivo IPL 2016** for sponsorship reasons) was the ninth season of the [Indian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Premier_League "Indian Premier League"), a professional [Twenty20 cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20_cricket "Twenty20 cricket") league established by the [Board of Control for Cricket in India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Control_for_Cricket_in_India "Board of Control for Cricket in India") (BCCI) in 2007. The season began on 9 April 2016 and concluded on 29 May 2016 with the playing of the finals match between [Royal Challengers Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Challengers_Bangalore "Royal Challengers Bangalore") and [Sunrisers Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunrisers_Hyderabad "Sunrisers Hyderabad") at [M. Chinnaswamy Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M._Chinnaswamy_Stadium "M. Chinnaswamy Stadium") in [Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangalore "Bangalore").

The 2016 season was the first IPL season to use LED [stumps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stump_(cricket) "Stump (cricket)"). Following the suspension of [Chennai Super Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai_Super_Kings "Chennai Super Kings") and [Rajasthan Royals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajasthan_Royals "Rajasthan Royals") for two years over a [spot-fixing and betting case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Indian_Premier_League_spot-fixing_and_betting_case "2013 Indian Premier League spot-fixing and betting case") during the 2013 IPL season, the IPL allocated spots for two new franchises to take their place. The process would result in the establishment of the [Gujarat Lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat_Lions "Gujarat Lions") and [Rising Pune Supergiants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rising_Pune_Supergiants "Rising Pune Supergiants").

The championship was won by [Sunrisers Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunrisers_Hyderabad "Sunrisers Hyderabad"), marking the [Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyderabad "Hyderabad") franchise's second IPL title, with [Ben Cutting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Cutting "Ben Cutting") declared the man of the match in the final. [Virat Kohli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virat_Kohli "Virat Kohli") of [Royal Challengers Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Challengers_Bangalore "Royal Challengers Bangalore") was named the most valuable player of the tournament, and [Mustafizur Rahman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mustafizur_Rahman "Mustafizur Rahman") of Sunrisers Hyderabad was named the emerging player of the season. Kohli was the tournament's leading run-scorer with 973 runs and [Bhuvneshwar Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuvneshwar_Kumar "Bhuvneshwar Kumar") of [Sunrisers Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunrisers_Hyderabad "Sunrisers Hyderabad") was the leading wicket-taker of the tournament with 23 wickets. Ever since the introduction of [Page playoff system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Page_playoff_system "Page playoff system"), this is the only edition where a team ending outside of the top 2 at the end of league stage won an IPL title.

## Format

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Format")]

Eight teams contested the season. Two teams, [Rising Pune Supergiants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rising_Pune_Supergiants "Rising Pune Supergiants") and [Gujarat Lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat_Lions "Gujarat Lions"), based in [Pune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pune "Pune") and [Rajkot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajkot "Rajkot") were new to the tournament, replacing the [Chennai Super Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai_Super_Kings "Chennai Super Kings") and [Rajasthan Royals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajasthan_Royals "Rajasthan Royals") franchises which had been suspended until 2018.

The schedule for the tournament was published on 10 March 2016. The league stage, consisting of 56 matches, took place between 9 April and 22 May 2016. The top four teams qualified for the play-off stage, with the final being held in [Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangalore "Bangalore") on 29 May.

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Background")]

On 14 July 2015, the RM Lodha committee suspended the owners of the [Chennai Super Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai_Super_Kings "Chennai Super Kings") and [Rajasthan Royals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajasthan_Royals "Rajasthan Royals") franchises for a period of two years on charges of [spot-fixing and betting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Indian_Premier_League_spot-fixing_and_betting_case "2013 Indian Premier League spot-fixing and betting case") during the 2013 IPL season. This meant that the two teams could not play in the 2016 and 2017 IPL seasons.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-1) The [Board of Control of Cricket in India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Control_of_Cricket_in_India "Board of Control of Cricket in India") (BCCI) confirmed that two new teams will replace them for the next two seasons of the IPL.

In October 2015, [PepsiCo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PepsiCo "PepsiCo") withdrew as the title sponsor of the IPL, terminating a five-year deal which was to end in 2017. Chinese smartphone manufacturer [Vivo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivo_(smartphone) "Vivo (smartphone)") was awarded the title sponsorship for the 2016 and 2017 seasons.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-2)

In November 2015, the BCCI shortlisted nine cities for the new franchises to be based in, leaving out [Jaipur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaipur "Jaipur") (home of Rajasthan Royals) and [Kochi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kochi "Kochi") (home of the now defunct [Kochi Tuskers Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kochi_Tuskers_Kerala "Kochi Tuskers Kerala")) for unknown reasons.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-dec8-3) The nine cities shortlisted were: [Chennai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai "Chennai"), [Cuttack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuttack "Cuttack"), [Dharamshala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharamshala "Dharamshala"), [Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore"), [Nagpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagpur "Nagpur"), [Pune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pune "Pune"), [Rajkot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajkot "Rajkot"), [Ranchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranchi "Ranchi") and [Visakhapatnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visakhapatnam "Visakhapatnam").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-4) The new franchises were allocated using a reverse auction process, with companies which bid the lowest share of the central revenue pool becoming the owners of the new teams.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-dec8-3) On 3 December, it was reported that twelve companies collected tender documents for the bidding process.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-eco-5)

On 8 December 2015, it was announced that New Rising, a company led by [Sanjiv Goenka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjiv_Goenka "Sanjiv Goenka"), and [Intex Technologies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intex_Technologies "Intex Technologies") had won the bidding rights to the two new teams. New Rising decided to have their team based in [Pune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rising_Pune_Supergiants "Rising Pune Supergiants") while Intex chose [Rajkot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat_Lions "Gujarat Lions") as the home of its team.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-Teams_Announced-6) The two franchises picked five players each from the squads of Chennai Super Kings and Rajasthan Royals at a player draft on 15 December 2015. Each franchise was allocated a purse of ₹660 million to buy the players for their squad at the draft and players auction.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-eco-5)

### Maharashtra water crisis

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Maharashtra water crisis")]

On 6 April 2016, amid a severe drought situation in the state of [Maharashtra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharashtra "Maharashtra"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ciwater6apr16-7) in which three venues (Mumbai, Pune and Nagpur) were supposed to host a total of 20 IPL matches in the 2016 season, the [Bombay High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay_High_Court "Bombay High Court") questioned the "criminal wastage"[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-toiwater9apr16-8) of water being supplied to the three stadiums in a response to a petition from the [Lok Satta Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Satta_Movement "Lok Satta Movement") NGO.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-hindu7apr16-9) The drought was described as one of the "worst-ever droughts" to affect the state[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ciwater6apr16-7) and was believed to be one of the worst droughts in 100 years.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-bbc13apr16-10) An estimated 6 million litres (6 million litres)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-bbc13apr16-10) of water were to be used at the three venues to maintain the pitches, with 4 million litres being used at the [Wankhede Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wankhede_Stadium "Wankhede Stadium"), the site of eight matches.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-hindu7apr16-9)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-mmwater9apr16-11) The High Court filed a [public interest litigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_interest_litigation "Public interest litigation") and suggested shifting matches to "some other state where water is in abundance." The High Court questioned the [BCCI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Control_for_Cricket_in_India "Board of Control for Cricket in India") about whether "people are more important or your IPL matches".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-mmwater9apr16-11) The BCCI argued that the water being used at the venues was tanker water and not drinkable.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ciwater6apr16-7)

On 8 April, the Chief Minister of Maharashtra [Devendra Fadnavis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devendra_Fadnavis "Devendra Fadnavis") declared that potable water will not be supplied to the venues and added "even if IPL matches are shifted, we have no problem."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-toiwater9apr16-8) On 9 April, hours before the season's opening match, the [Mumbai Cricket Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai_Cricket_Association "Mumbai Cricket Association") claimed that the water being used at the Wankhede Stadium was bought from private operators and not [Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brihanmumbai_Municipal_Corporation "Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-tiewater9apr16-12)

On 13 April, the Bombay High Court ruled that all the matches to be held in the state in May must be moved to venues outside of Maharashtra. A total of 13 matches were scheduled to be hosted by the three venues in Maharashtra in the month of May, including two playoff matches in Pune and the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League_final "2016 Indian Premier League final") in Mumbai.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-bbc13apr16-10)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-moved-14) The court later allowed a match scheduled for 1 May to take place in Pune due to logistical difficulties with moving the fixture.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ci20apr16-15)

The Mumbai Cricket Association and the [Maharashtra Cricket Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharashtra_Cricket_Association "Maharashtra Cricket Association") petitioned the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_(India) "Supreme Court (India)") against the High Court's ruling, filing a plea which stated that treated sewage water will be used instead of potable water.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-mca-16) After the [Mumbai Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai_Indians "Mumbai Indians") selected [Jaipur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaipur "Jaipur") as their alternative venue, a petition was filed in the city which stated hosting IPL matches "will add unnecessary burden on the scarce natural resource."[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-17) The [Rajasthan High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajasthan_High_Court "Rajasthan High Court") then questioned the state government and BCCI about shifting the matches to [Rajasthan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajasthan "Rajasthan"), a region also hit by drought, scheduling the hearing for 27 April.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-18) There were reports of protests being held in Jaipur against the shifting of matches to the city.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-mca-16)

On 26 April the Supreme Court dismissed the petition against the Bombay High Court's ruling and confirmed that matches should be moved out of Maharashtra.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ie27apr16-19) The court had initially suggested that a series of regulations could be used to allow matches to go ahead under the condition that no drinkable water was used on the grounds, but opted to instead move the matches on the grounds that the suggested regulations would be complex and difficult to enforce.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ie27apr16-19)

On 29 April, it was announced that all league stage matches scheduled to be held after 1 May in Mumbai and Pune were shifted to the [Dr. Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy ACA-VDCA Cricket Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Y.S._Rajasekhara_Reddy_ACA-VDCA_Cricket_Stadium "Dr. Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy ACA-VDCA Cricket Stadium") in [Visakhapatnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visakhapatnam "Visakhapatnam"). Two playoff matches scheduled to be held in Pune were shifted to Delhi and three [Kings XI Punjab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kings_XI_Punjab "Kings XI Punjab") home matches supposed to be held in Nagpur were shifted to their primary home venue, Mohali. The [M. Chinnaswamy Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M._Chinnaswamy_Stadium "M. Chinnaswamy Stadium") in Bangalore, which was scheduled to host the Qualifier 1, was also announced as the host of the Final.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-vizag-20)

## Opening ceremony

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Opening ceremony")]

The opening ceremony was held on 8 April 2016 from 19:30 IST at the [Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sardar_Vallabhbhai_Patel_Indoor_Stadium "Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Indoor Stadium") in Mumbai. It featured performances from [Major Lazer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_Lazer "Major Lazer"), [Yo Yo Honey Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yo_Yo_Honey_Singh "Yo Yo Honey Singh"), [Ranveer Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranveer_Singh "Ranveer Singh"), [Katrina Kaif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katrina_Kaif "Katrina Kaif"), [Jacqueline Fernandez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacqueline_Fernandez "Jacqueline Fernandez") among others.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-21)[Dwayne Bravo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwayne_Bravo "Dwayne Bravo"), a member of the West Indies' [2016 World Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_World_Twenty20 "2016 World Twenty20") winning team, performed the "Champion Dance", which, according to the IPL chairman [Rajeev Shukla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajeev_Shukla "Rajeev Shukla"), was supposed to be the "special attraction" of the ceremony.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-ie-22)

Venues used during the season

Ten venues were selected to host the league stage matches.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-23)[Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangalore "Bangalore") hosted Qualifier 1, [Pune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pune "Pune") was scheduled to host the Eliminator match and Qualifier 2 and [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai") was scheduled to host the final.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-24) The drought situation in [Maharashtra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharashtra "Maharashtra") led to a ruling in the [Bombay High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay_High_Court "Bombay High Court") that games to be played in the state, including in Pune and Mumbai, in May would have to be moved to other regions to allow water supplies to be prioritised.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-bbc13apr16-10) On 29 April 2016, the IPL Governing Council announced that all homes games of the Mumbai Indians and Rising Pune Supergiants after 2 May 2016, would be held at [Visakhapatnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visakhapatnam "Visakhapatnam"). The Eliminator and Qualifier 2 would to be held at [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi"), and the final at [Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangalore "Bangalore").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-vizag-20) On 2 May 2016, it was announced that Gujarat Lions would play two of their matches on 19 and 21 May at [Kanpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanpur "Kanpur").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League#cite_note-25)

## Personnel changes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_Indian_Premier_League&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personnel changes")]

Main article: [List of 2016 Indian Premier League personnel changes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_2016_Indian_Premier_League_personnel_changes "List of 2016 Indian Premier League personnel changes")

Each franchise was able to retain players from the previous season of the tournament, with their salaries automatically deducted from the franchise's available salary purse. The new teams were able to draft five players each from the two suspended franchises. Players were able to be traded during the trading windows and new players could be added to the teams at the 2016 IPL players auction held on 6 February 2016.

Umpire Oxenford had no hesitation. **71/3** **16.1 to Q de Kock,**another wicket. Daredevils falling away quickly. Flatter delivery outside off, de Kock backs away and flat-bats a stroke to Jordan at long-off. The umpires want to check if Chahal has overstepped, very marginal call. **Umeshkumar Tilak Yadav** (born 25 October 1987) is an Indian [cricketer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") who represented the [Indian cricket team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_national_cricket_team "India national cricket team"). He currently plays for [Vidarbha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vidarbha_cricket_team "Vidarbha cricket team") in domestic cricket. He played 57 [test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Test_cricket "Test cricket") matches for India and his [fast-bowling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_bowling "Fast bowling") contributed of India winning test matches particularly at home. Yadav was a member of the team that won the [2013 ICC Champions Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_ICC_Champions_Trophy "2013 ICC Champions Trophy"). He was the highest wicket-taker for India in the [2015 Cricket World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Cricket_World_Cup "2015 Cricket World Cup").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-1)

A right-arm fast bowler, Yadav has played for Vidarbha at domestic level since 2008 and is the first player from the team to have played Test cricket. He made his [One Day International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Day_International "One Day International") (ODI) debut against [Zimbabwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe_national_cricket_team "Zimbabwe national cricket team") in May 2010. The following year, in November, Yadav made his Test debut against the [West Indies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Indies_cricket_team "West Indies cricket team"). He holds the record of the [highest strike rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strike_rate "Strike rate") in an innings in Test cricket after scoring 31 runs in 10 balls at a strike rate of 310 against South Africa in October 2019.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-2)

## Personal life and domestic career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Umesh_Yadav&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Personal life and domestic career")]

Before becoming a professional cricketer, Umesh unsuccessfully applied to join the army and the police force. Yadav tried to make a place in his college cricket team but was refused because he did not play for any club. Then, in the year 2007, having previously only ever played tennis ball cricket, Yadav joined Vidarbha Gymkhana (club affiliated to VCA; established in 1969 by J.A. Karnewar) and first time began bowling with a leather ball in Guzder League 'A' Division cricket tournament organised by Vidarbha Cricket Association (VCA). [Pritam Gandhe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pritam_Gandhe "Pritam Gandhe"), Vidharbha's Ranji trophy team captain, supported Yadav and ensured he represented Air India in a [Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20 "Twenty20") tournament. Of Yadav's early career, Gandhe remarked: "He was raw and wayward. But he was really quick– too quick. I thought that if he lands at least three out of six balls in line with the stumps, he will trouble batsmen."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-fast_track-3)

On 3 November 2008, Yadav made his [first-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-class_cricket "First-class cricket") debut for [Vidarbha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vidarbha_cricket_team "Vidarbha cricket team") against [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh_cricket_team "Madhya Pradesh cricket team") in the [2008–09 Ranji Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_Ranji_Trophy "2008–09 Ranji Trophy"). His first wicket was that of Himalaya Sagar who was out bowled; Yadav did not bowl in Madhya Pradesh' second innings, but in the first claimed four wickets for 72 runs (4/75) as his team lost by ten wickets.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-4) He played in four of Vidarbha's Ranji matches that season, taking 20 wickets at an average of 14.60 with best figures of 6/105.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-6) Also in the 2008/09 season, Yadav made his [one-day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_A "List A") debut.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-7)

From playing for Vidarbha, Yadav was selected to represent the [Central Zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Zone_cricket_team "Central Zone cricket team") in the [Duleep Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duleep_Trophy "Duleep Trophy") in his first season.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-fast_track-3)

On 16 April 2013, Umesh got engaged to Delhi-based fashion designer Tanya Wadhwa, and they were married on 29 May 2013. The couple have two daughters born in January 2021 and March 2023 respectively. Initially Umesh had troubled family life as his brother was acquitted in a robbery case.In his early years he moved from Jharkhand to Nagpur.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-9)

In January 2019, in the first semi-final of [2018/19 Ranji Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Ranji_Trophy#Semi-finals "2018–19 Ranji Trophy") against [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_cricket_team "Kerala cricket team"), he gave his career-best performance of 7/48 in the first innings and then returned with figures of 5/31 in the second innings, and ended the match with career-best figures of 12/79 which sailed Vidarbha to the Ranji Trophy final.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-11)

### Indian Premier League

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Umesh_Yadav&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Indian Premier League")]

Umesh was signed by [Delhi Daredevils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi_Daredevils "Delhi Daredevils") in 2010 and played for the franchise for four seasons. He was the fourth highest wicket-taker in the [2012 IPL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_IPL "2012 IPL") with 19 wickets from 17 matches at an average of 23.84.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-13)

Ahead of the [2014 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_IPL "2014 IPL"), Umesh was bought by [Kolkata Knight Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Knight_Riders "Kolkata Knight Riders").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-14) He played for the team for four season before being released ahead of the [2018 IPL auction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_IPL_auction "2018 IPL auction")[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-15) during which he was bought by [Royal Challengers Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Challengers_Bangalore "Royal Challengers Bangalore").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-16) He took 20 wickets from 14 matches in 2018.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-iplt20.com-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-19) In 2019 he took eight 8 wickets from 11 matches[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-iplt20.com-17) and in 2020 only played in two matches.[_[why?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_][[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-iplt20.com-17)

Umesh was released by RCB ahead of the [2021 IPL auction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_IPL_auction "2021 IPL auction")[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-20) and was bought by Delhi.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-21) In February 2022, he was bought by the [Kolkata Knight Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Knight_Riders "Kolkata Knight Riders") in the [auction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_2022_Indian_Premier_League_personnel_changes "List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes") for the [2022 Indian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Indian_Premier_League "2022 Indian Premier League") tournament.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-22) In 2022 he gave best performance of his IPL career by taking 4 wicket against Punjab Kings. In 2024, he will play for Gujarat Titans after being released by KKR.

## International career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Umesh_Yadav&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: International career")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/74/Umesh_Yadav%2C_Wasim_Akram.jpg/250px-Umesh_Yadav%2C_Wasim_Akram.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Umesh_Yadav,_Wasim_Akram.jpg)

Umesh Yadav (left) and [Wasim Akram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wasim_Akram "Wasim Akram") (right), in a training session in [IPL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Premier_League "Indian Premier League") (2014) 

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/Manish_Pandey%2C_Umesh_Yadav.jpg/250px-Manish_Pandey%2C_Umesh_Yadav.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Manish_Pandey,_Umesh_Yadav.jpg)

[Manish Pandey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manish_Pandey "Manish Pandey") (left) and Umesh Yadav (right), in an ad during IPL 2015

In May 2010, Yadav was called into India's squad for the [World Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_ICC_World_Twenty20 "2010 ICC World Twenty20") in place of the injured [Praveen Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Praveen_Kumar_(cricketer) "Praveen Kumar (cricketer)"),[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-23) but did not go on to play in the tournament. Later that month, he was included in the squad to play a [tri-nation ODI series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tri-nation_series_in_Zimbabwe_in_2010 "Tri-nation series in Zimbabwe in 2010") in Zimbabwe against the hosts and [Sri Lanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Lanka_national_cricket_team "Sri Lanka national cricket team"). India sent an under-strength squad with nine first-choice players either rested or injured.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-24) Yadav made his ODI debut in the tournament during India's loss to Zimbabwe, a team ranked tenth by the ICC at the time. Defending a score of 285, Yadav bowled eight wicketless overs while conceding 48 runs.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-27) Playing in three matches, Yadav took a single wicket.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-28)

After the tri-series in Zimbabwe, Yadav returned to the fringes of the team. He was included as a practice bowler when India toured Sri Lanka in July to gain experience of bowling to [Test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Test_cricket "Test cricket") batsmen.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-29) He would have to wait until October 2011 before his next international match.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-30) After India toured South Africa in [December 2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_cricket_team_in_South_Africa_in_2010%E2%80%9311 "Indian cricket team in South Africa in 2010–11"), Yadav was dropped out of the national squad.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-return2011-31)

Yadav returned to the national set-up in September 2011 for a [five-match ODI series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_cricket_team_in_India_in_2011%E2%80%9312 "English cricket team in India in 2011–12") against [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England_cricket_team "England cricket team").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-return2011-31) An injury to his left hand meant Yadav missed the last two ODIs. At times expensive though regularly fast,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-32) he managed four wickets at an [average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowling_average "Bowling average") of 38.25 from three matches.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-33)

When the [West Indies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Indies_cricket_team "West Indies cricket team") toured in November 2011, the Indian selectors opted to change the team's fast bowlers. [Sreesanth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sreesanth "Sreesanth") and [Praveen Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Praveen_Kumar_(cricketer) "Praveen Kumar (cricketer)") were left out of the squad and Yadav and [Varun Aaron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varun_Aaron "Varun Aaron") were chosen based on their performances in the ODIs against England earlier that year.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-34) Yadav made his Test debut in the first match and opened the bowling alongside [Ishant Sharma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ishant_Sharma "Ishant Sharma") in the first innings, though failed to take a wicket. In the second innings, the [spinners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_bowling "Spin bowling") opened the bowling and Yadav took two wickets for 36 runs (2/36) to help India to a five-wicket victory.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-35) Yadav was the first cricketer to play for Vidarbha who went on the play Test cricket.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-fast_track-3) India also won the second Test,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-36) and Yadav finished with nine wickets in the series, the most amongst India's fast bowlers and less than half the total of either of the team's spinners.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-37) In the [five-match ODI series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Indian_cricket_team_in_India_in_2011%E2%80%9312#ODI_Series "West Indian cricket team in India in 2011–12") that followed, he managed six wickets at an average of 24.33 from three appearances.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-38)

Yadav was selected as one of India's pace bowlers for their [tour of Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_cricket_team_in_Australia_in_2011%E2%80%9312 "Indian cricket team in Australia in 2011–12") in 2011–12. He played in all four Tests, taking 14 wickets at an average of 39.35 as India lost the series 4–0.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-39) In the third Test at the [WACA Ground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WACA_Ground "WACA Ground") in [Perth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perth "Perth"), he took his first five-wicket haul in Test cricket, with figures of 5/93 in Australia's first and only innings.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-40) In the triangular ODI series with Australia and Sri Lanka that followed, Yadav managed 5 wickets from 6 matches at an average of 59.80.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-41)

In May 2013, Umesh was named in India's 15 member squad for the [2013 ICC Champions Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_ICC_Champions_Trophy "2013 ICC Champions Trophy").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-43) He didn't have a great tournament as he had picked up just 4 wickets from all the 5 matches that he played in the tournament.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-44)

In December 2014, Umesh was named in India's 20 member squad for the [2015 Cricket World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Cricket_World_Cup "2015 Cricket World Cup").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-46) He was India's highest wicket-taker in the tournament with 18 wickets from 8 matches and was also the third highest wicket-taker in the tournament.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-47)

In May 2021, Umesh was named in India's 20 member Test squad for India's [World Test Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Test_Championship "World Test Championship") final against New Zealand and for India's 4 match Test series [against England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_cricket_team_in_England_in_2021 "Indian cricket team in England in 2021").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-50)

## Bowling style

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Umesh_Yadav&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Bowling style")]

Umesh is the fastest Indian bowler with his top speed being 152.5 km/h. Writing for [ESPNcricinfo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPNcricinfo "ESPNcricinfo") in January 2012, Sidharth Monga commented that

> Yadav is fit, strong, quick, and gets the ball to swing late. More importantly, he attacks the stumps and doesn't wait for edges. Eleven of his 21 Test wickets have been bowled. Another has been lbw. Five matches is a short career for a bigger statistical analysis, but it is worth mentioning that he takes a wicket every 39.2 balls. It is not at large odds with his overall first-class strike-rate of 46.8. Attacking the stumps also leaves less control on the run flow, which shows in his economy rate of 4.24 in Tests.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-51)

Former Australian bowler [Glenn McGrath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_McGrath "Glenn McGrath") was impressed with Yadav's performance in the first Test at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in January. McGrath said

> He was quite impressive. He bowls at a good pace. He seems to have a great attitude and most importantly, he's a wicket-taking bowler. Perhaps, the direction and control are not there quite yet, but it's not far away. He's got that raw talent, good pace and can generate good bounce. He's got a lot going for him at the moment.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-52)

Former Indian cricketer Aakash Chopra, impressed by Umesh's performance in the [Border–Gavaskar Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Border%E2%80%93Gavaskar_Trophy "Border–Gavaskar Trophy") in 2017, said,

"It's not often that you see an Indian seamer outpace and outbowl his Australian counterparts but the spell that sealed the deal for India in Dharamshala did just that. Umesh Yadav bowled with a lot of steam on the third-day pitch and dismissed both openers before half the lead was wiped out. There are certain spells in Test matches that leave an indelible mark on one’s memory and his spell in Dharamshala will go down as one of them."[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-53)

**Umeshkumar Tilak Yadav** (born 25 October 1987) is an Indian [cricketer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") who represented the [Indian cricket team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_national_cricket_team "India national cricket team"). He currently plays for [Vidarbha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vidarbha_cricket_team "Vidarbha cricket team") in domestic cricket. He played 57 [test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Test_cricket "Test cricket") matches for India and his [fast-bowling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_bowling "Fast bowling") contributed of India winning test matches particularly at home. Yadav was a member of the team that won the [2013 ICC Champions Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_ICC_Champions_Trophy "2013 ICC Champions Trophy"). He was the highest wicket-taker for India in the [2015 Cricket World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Cricket_World_Cup "2015 Cricket World Cup").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-1)

A right-arm fast bowler, Yadav has played for Vidarbha at domestic level since 2008 and is the first player from the team to have played Test cricket. He made his [One Day International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Day_International "One Day International") (ODI) debut against [Zimbabwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe_national_cricket_team "Zimbabwe national cricket team") in May 2010. The following year, in November, Yadav made his Test debut against the [West Indies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Indies_cricket_team "West Indies cricket team"). He holds the record of the [highest strike rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strike_rate "Strike rate") in an innings in Test cricket after scoring 31 runs in 10 balls at a strike rate of 310 against South Africa in October 2019.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-2)

## Personal life and domestic career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Umesh_Yadav&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Personal life and domestic career")]

Before becoming a professional cricketer, Umesh unsuccessfully applied to join the army and the police force. Yadav tried to make a place in his college cricket team but was refused because he did not play for any club. Then, in the year 2007, having previously only ever played tennis ball cricket, Yadav joined Vidarbha Gymkhana (club affiliated to VCA; established in 1969 by J.A. Karnewar) and first time began bowling with a leather ball in Guzder League 'A' Division cricket tournament organised by Vidarbha Cricket Association (VCA). [Pritam Gandhe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pritam_Gandhe "Pritam Gandhe"), Vidharbha's Ranji trophy team captain, supported Yadav and ensured he represented Air India in a [Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20 "Twenty20") tournament. Of Yadav's early career, Gandhe remarked: "He was raw and wayward. But he was really quick– too quick. I thought that if he lands at least three out of six balls in line with the stumps, he will trouble batsmen."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-fast_track-3)

On 3 November 2008, Yadav made his [first-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-class_cricket "First-class cricket") debut for [Vidarbha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vidarbha_cricket_team "Vidarbha cricket team") against [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh_cricket_team "Madhya Pradesh cricket team") in the [2008–09 Ranji Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_Ranji_Trophy "2008–09 Ranji Trophy"). His first wicket was that of Himalaya Sagar who was out bowled; Yadav did not bowl in Madhya Pradesh' second innings, but in the first claimed four wickets for 72 runs (4/75) as his team lost by ten wickets.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-4) He played in four of Vidarbha's Ranji matches that season, taking 20 wickets at an average of 14.60 with best figures of 6/105.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-6) Also in the 2008/09 season, Yadav made his [one-day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_A "List A") debut.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-7)

From playing for Vidarbha, Yadav was selected to represent the [Central Zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Zone_cricket_team "Central Zone cricket team") in the [Duleep Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duleep_Trophy "Duleep Trophy") in his first season.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-fast_track-3)

On 16 April 2013, Umesh got engaged to Delhi-based fashion designer Tanya Wadhwa, and they were married on 29 May 2013. The couple have two daughters born in January 2021 and March 2023 respectively. Initially Umesh had troubled family life as his brother was acquitted in a robbery case.In his early years he moved from Jharkhand to Nagpur.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-9)

In January 2019, in the first semi-final of [2018/19 Ranji Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Ranji_Trophy#Semi-finals "2018–19 Ranji Trophy") against [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_cricket_team "Kerala cricket team"), he gave his career-best performance of 7/48 in the first innings and then returned with figures of 5/31 in the second innings, and ended the match with career-best figures of 12/79 which sailed Vidarbha to the Ranji Trophy final.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-11)

### Indian Premier League

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Umesh_Yadav&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Indian Premier League")]

Umesh was signed by [Delhi Daredevils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi_Daredevils "Delhi Daredevils") in 2010 and played for the franchise for four seasons. He was the fourth highest wicket-taker in the [2012 IPL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_IPL "2012 IPL") with 19 wickets from 17 matches at an average of 23.84.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-13)

Ahead of the [2014 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_IPL "2014 IPL"), Umesh was bought by [Kolkata Knight Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Knight_Riders "Kolkata Knight Riders").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-14) He played for the team for four season before being released ahead of the [2018 IPL auction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_IPL_auction "2018 IPL auction")[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-15) during which he was bought by [Royal Challengers Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Challengers_Bangalore "Royal Challengers Bangalore").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-16) He took 20 wickets from 14 matches in 2018.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-iplt20.com-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-19) In 2019 he took eight 8 wickets from 11 matches[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-iplt20.com-17) and in 2020 only played in two matches.[_[why?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_][[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-iplt20.com-17)

Umesh was released by RCB ahead of the [2021 IPL auction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_IPL_auction "2021 IPL auction")[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-20) and was bought by Delhi.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-21) In February 2022, he was bought by the [Kolkata Knight Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Knight_Riders "Kolkata Knight Riders") in the [auction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_2022_Indian_Premier_League_personnel_changes "List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes") for the [2022 Indian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Indian_Premier_League "2022 Indian Premier League") tournament.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-22) In 2022 he gave best performance of his IPL career by taking 4 wicket against Punjab Kings. In 2024, he will play for Gujarat Titans after being released by KKR.

## International career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Umesh_Yadav&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: International career")]

In May 2010, Yadav was called into India's squad for the [World Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_ICC_World_Twenty20 "2010 ICC World Twenty20") in place of the injured [Praveen Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Praveen_Kumar_(cricketer) "Praveen Kumar (cricketer)"),[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-23) but did not go on to play in the tournament. Later that month, he was included in the squad to play a [tri-nation ODI series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tri-nation_series_in_Zimbabwe_in_2010 "Tri-nation series in Zimbabwe in 2010") in Zimbabwe against the hosts and [Sri Lanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Lanka_national_cricket_team "Sri Lanka national cricket team"). India sent an under-strength squad with nine first-choice players either rested or injured.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-24) Yadav made his ODI debut in the tournament during India's loss to Zimbabwe, a team ranked tenth by the ICC at the time. Defending a score of 285, Yadav bowled eight wicketless overs while conceding 48 runs.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-27) Playing in three matches, Yadav took a single wicket.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-28)

After the tri-series in Zimbabwe, Yadav returned to the fringes of the team. He was included as a practice bowler when India toured Sri Lanka in July to gain experience of bowling to [Test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Test_cricket "Test cricket") batsmen.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-29) He would have to wait until October 2011 before his next international match.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-30) After India toured South Africa in [December 2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_cricket_team_in_South_Africa_in_2010%E2%80%9311 "Indian cricket team in South Africa in 2010–11"), Yadav was dropped out of the national squad.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-return2011-31)

Yadav returned to the national set-up in September 2011 for a [five-match ODI series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_cricket_team_in_India_in_2011%E2%80%9312 "English cricket team in India in 2011–12") against [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England_cricket_team "England cricket team").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-return2011-31) An injury to his left hand meant Yadav missed the last two ODIs. At times expensive though regularly fast,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-32) he managed four wickets at an [average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowling_average "Bowling average") of 38.25 from three matches.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-33)

When the [West Indies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Indies_cricket_team "West Indies cricket team") toured in November 2011, the Indian selectors opted to change the team's fast bowlers. [Sreesanth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sreesanth "Sreesanth") and [Praveen Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Praveen_Kumar_(cricketer) "Praveen Kumar (cricketer)") were left out of the squad and Yadav and [Varun Aaron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varun_Aaron "Varun Aaron") were chosen based on their performances in the ODIs against England earlier that year.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-34) Yadav made his Test debut in the first match and opened the bowling alongside [Ishant Sharma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ishant_Sharma "Ishant Sharma") in the first innings, though failed to take a wicket. In the second innings, the [spinners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_bowling "Spin bowling") opened the bowling and Yadav took two wickets for 36 runs (2/36) to help India to a five-wicket victory.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-35) Yadav was the first cricketer to play for Vidarbha who went on the play Test cricket.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-fast_track-3) India also won the second Test,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-36) and Yadav finished with nine wickets in the series, the most amongst India's fast bowlers and less than half the total of either of the team's spinners.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-37) In the [five-match ODI series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Indian_cricket_team_in_India_in_2011%E2%80%9312#ODI_Series "West Indian cricket team in India in 2011–12") that followed, he managed six wickets at an average of 24.33 from three appearances.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-38)

Yadav was selected as one of India's pace bowlers for their [tour of Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_cricket_team_in_Australia_in_2011%E2%80%9312 "Indian cricket team in Australia in 2011–12") in 2011–12. He played in all four Tests, taking 14 wickets at an average of 39.35 as India lost the series 4–0.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-39) In the third Test at the [WACA Ground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WACA_Ground "WACA Ground") in [Perth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perth "Perth"), he took his first five-wicket haul in Test cricket, with figures of 5/93 in Australia's first and only innings.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-40) In the triangular ODI series with Australia and Sri Lanka that followed, Yadav managed 5 wickets from 6 matches at an average of 59.80.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-41)

In May 2013, Umesh was named in India's 15 member squad for the [2013 ICC Champions Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_ICC_Champions_Trophy "2013 ICC Champions Trophy").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-43) He didn't have a great tournament as he had picked up just 4 wickets from all the 5 matches that he played in the tournament.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-44)

In December 2014, Umesh was named in India's 20 member squad for the [2015 Cricket World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Cricket_World_Cup "2015 Cricket World Cup").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-46) He was India's highest wicket-taker in the tournament with 18 wickets from 8 matches and was also the third highest wicket-taker in the tournament.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-47)

In May 2021, Umesh was named in India's 20 member Test squad for India's [World Test Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Test_Championship "World Test Championship") final against New Zealand and for India's 4 match Test series [against England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_cricket_team_in_England_in_2021 "Indian cricket team in England in 2021").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-50)

## Bowling style

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Umesh_Yadav&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Bowling style")]

Umesh is the fastest Indian bowler with his top speed being 152.5 km/h. Writing for [ESPNcricinfo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPNcricinfo "ESPNcricinfo") in January 2012, Sidharth Monga commented that

> Yadav is fit, strong, quick, and gets the ball to swing late. More importantly, he attacks the stumps and doesn't wait for edges. Eleven of his 21 Test wickets have been bowled. Another has been lbw. Five matches is a short career for a bigger statistical analysis, but it is worth mentioning that he takes a wicket every 39.2 balls. It is not at large odds with his overall first-class strike-rate of 46.8. Attacking the stumps also leaves less control on the run flow, which shows in his economy rate of 4.24 in Tests.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-51)

Former Australian bowler [Glenn McGrath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_McGrath "Glenn McGrath") was impressed with Yadav's performance in the first Test at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in January. McGrath said

> He was quite impressive. He bowls at a good pace. He seems to have a great attitude and most importantly, he's a wicket-taking bowler. Perhaps, the direction and control are not there quite yet, but it's not far away. He's got that raw talent, good pace and can generate good bounce. He's got a lot going for him at the moment.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-52)

Former Indian cricketer Aakash Chopra, impressed by Umesh's performance in the [Border–Gavaskar Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Border%E2%80%93Gavaskar_Trophy "Border–Gavaskar Trophy") in 2017, said,

"It's not often that you see an Indian seamer outpace and outbowl his Australian counterparts but the spell that sealed the deal for India in Dharamshala did just that. Umesh Yadav bowled with a lot of steam on the third-day pitch and dismissed both openers before half the lead was wiped out. There are certain spells in Test matches that leave an indelible mark on one’s memory and his spell in Dharamshala will go down as one of them."[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Yadav#cite_note-53)
